process_name: Opening a Personal Bank Account in China
steps: Choose a bank and the account's payment or savings purpose
Visit a supported branch or begin through a bank's available digital channel
Provide a resident identity card; foreign nationals generally provide a passport or permanent-residence card
Provide supporting identity, residence, tax, or contact information if the bank cannot complete verification from the primary document
Complete real-name and customer-due-diligence checks
Fund the account if the product requires an opening deposit
Activate the bank card and mobile-payment or online-banking services offered
typical_requirements: Supporting proof of address or identity if requested
notes: Chinese banks must verify the applicant, the identity document, and the applicant's genuine intention to open the account. Exact supporting documents and digital-channel access vary by bank and customer status.

sources.title: Beijing government guide to personal bank-account identification
People's Bank of China settlement-account rules

process_name: Opening a Personal Deposit Account in Mexico
steps: Choose a traditional or simplified deposit account based on the transactions and balances you expect
Check whether the institution supports branch or digital opening for that product
Complete the application with personal, contact, occupation, and residence information requested by the bank
Provide valid official identification and CURP when required
Provide proof of address when required for the selected account level
Fund the account if the product has an opening minimum
Receive the debit card and CLABE used for transfers
typical_requirements: Proof of address for some accounts
notes: CONDUSEF distinguishes simplified accounts with lower information requirements and traditional accounts with fuller customer files. Limits and accepted documents depend on the account level and institution.

sources.title: CONDUSEF guidance on opening deposit accounts

process_name: Opening a Personal Payment Account in Vietnam
steps: Choose a bank and decide whether you need a payment account, savings deposit, or both
Check whether the bank supports branch or electronic opening for your customer type
Complete the bank's account-opening application and register customer information
Provide the current identity document required for your citizenship or residence status
Complete identity verification and any required biometric matching
Provide address, contact, and account-purpose information requested by the bank
Activate the payment card and digital-banking services available
notes: Identity-document rules changed for Vietnamese citizens from January 2026, so older guides referring to domestic passport use may be outdated. Confirm the current document and biometric requirements with the chosen bank.

sources.title: Vietnam government notice on 2026 bank identity rules
State Bank of Vietnam account-opening regulation

process_name: Opening a Personal Bank Account in South Korea
steps: Choose a bank and account type
Check whether the account must be opened at a branch or supports a digital channel
Provide a resident registration card or the identity documents applicable to your residence status
Provide a Korean address and contact information when requested
Explain and document the financial purpose of the account, such as salary receipt
Open a transaction-limited account if full purpose documentation is not yet available
Apply for a card and digital banking, then provide later evidence if needed to lift limits
typical_requirements: Signature or seal as accepted by the bank
notes: Korean banks may open an initially restricted account when transaction-purpose evidence is incomplete. Documents and limits vary by bank, account, and residence status.

process_name: Opening a Personal Deposit Account in El Salvador
steps: Choose between a regular savings, current, term, or simplified-requirements account
Compare each institution's opening minimum, fees, and available channels
Apply at a branch or through the bank's supported digital channel
Provide the identity and contact information required for that account type
Complete the institution's customer verification
Make the opening deposit when required
Activate the debit card, transfers, and digital banking included with the product
typical_requirements: Documento Único de Identidad or other accepted ID
Additional KYC information for regular accounts
notes: The SSF notes that requirements and minimum deposits vary by institution. A simplified-requirements savings account can generally be opened with minimal identification and has special limits disclosed by the bank.

sources.title: SSF guidance on simplified and regular savings accounts

process_name: Opening a Personal Deposit Account in the Dominican Republic
steps: Choose a savings, current, basic, or fixed-term product
Check whether the product supports online opening or requires a branch
Complete and sign the account application
Provide a cédula or passport as accepted for the product and customer status
Provide income information and additional customer-due-diligence documents when requested
Make the minimum opening deposit if the product requires one
Activate the debit card and digital-banking access offered
notes: Requirements differ between standard and basic/inclusive accounts and between residents and non-residents. Institutions may request additional documents to identify the customer and source of funds.

process_name: Opening a Personal Bank Account in the United Kingdom
steps: Compare current accounts, basic bank accounts, and savings accounts
Choose a bank or building society and check its application channels
Complete the application with personal, contact, tax-residency, and account-purpose information
Provide acceptable proof of identity
Provide proof of address if requested by the institution
Complete identity, fraud-prevention, and eligibility checks
Activate the debit card, online banking, and payment instructions
typical_requirements: Proof of identity, such as a passport or accepted identity card
notes: UK government guidance notes that banks may ask for proof of address, although it is not itself a legal prerequisite to opening every bank account. Basic bank accounts may offer alternative identity-evidence routes.

sources.title: GOV.UK guidance on opening a UK bank account
